lessons.summary: Win over your partner’s parents at their first family dinner.

content.title: Meeting the parents
content.scenario: Win over your partner’s parents at their first family dinner.

rounds.situation: You arrive at your partner’s parents’ flat with a gift.
rounds.cantonese: 伯父伯母，你哋好！呢啲係我帶嚟嘅少少心意。
rounds.jyutping: baak3 fu2 baak3 mou5 nei5 dei6 hou2 ni1 di1 hai6 ngo5 daai3 lai4 ge3 siu2 siu2 sam1 ji3
rounds.translation: Uncle, Auntie, hello! This is a little something I brought for you.

chunks.note: The respectful way to address a partner’s parents. Never use their first names.

chunks.jyutping: ni1 di1 hai6 ngo5 daai3 lai4 ge3
chunks.note: Hand the gift over with both hands as you say it.
Always play a gift down. Calling it 少少心意 sounds modest and warm.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Greet your partner’s parents and hand over your gift modestly.

rounds.situation: They insist on fussing over you at the door.
rounds.cantonese: 唔使客氣，我除咗鞋先入嚟。
rounds.jyutping: m4 sai2 haak3 hei3 ngo5 ceoi4 zo2 haai4 sin1 jap6 lai4
rounds.translation: No need to fuss, I’ll take my shoes off before coming in.

chunks.note: Hosts in Hong Kong love to fuss over guests. This line politely waves it off.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 ceoi4 zo2 haai4 sin1 jap6 lai4
chunks.english: I’ll take my shoes off before coming in
chunks.note: 先 at the end means “first”: do this before the next thing.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell them not to fuss and that you’ll take your shoes off first.

rounds.situation: Dinner is served. Praise Auntie’s cooking.
rounds.cantonese: 伯母煮嘅餸好好味呀，好似酒樓咁！
rounds.jyutping: baak3 mou5 zyu2 ge3 sung3 hou2 hou2 mei6 aa3 hou2 ci5 zau2 lau4 gam3
rounds.translation: Auntie, your cooking is so delicious, just like a restaurant!

chunks.note: 餸 means the dishes you eat with rice. Every home cook loves hearing about theirs.
Doubling 好 makes the praise warmer. 呀 keeps it friendly.
好似…咁 means “just like…”. Comparing home food to a 酒樓 is high praise.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Compliment the food and compare it to a restaurant.

rounds.situation: Uncle asks what you do for a living.
rounds.cantonese: 我而家喺一間設計公司做嘢，做咗三年喇。
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 hai2 jat1 gaan1 cit3 gai3 gung1 si1 zou6 je5 zou6 zo2 saam1 nin4 laa3
rounds.translation: I work at a design company now; it’s been three years.

chunks.cantonese: 我而家喺一間設計公司做嘢
chunks.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 hai2 jat1 gaan1 cit3 gai3 gung1 si1 zou6 je5
chunks.english: I work at a design company now
chunks.note: 喺 + place + 做嘢 is the everyday way to say where you work.
咗 + time + 喇 says how long something has been going on. Parents like hearing you’re stable.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell Uncle where you work and for how long.

rounds.situation: It’s time to leave. Thank them and offer to return the favour.
rounds.cantonese: 多謝你哋招呼，下次到我請你哋飲茶！
rounds.jyutping: do1 ze6 nei5 dei6 ziu1 fu1 haa6 ci3 dou3 ngo5 ceng2 nei5 dei6 jam2 caa4
rounds.translation: Thanks for having me. Next time, dim sum’s on me!

chunks.jyutping: do1 ze6 nei5 dei6 ziu1 fu1
chunks.note: 多謝 thanks someone for a gift or kindness. 招呼 means looking after a guest.
到我 means “my turn”. Offering to repay the favour is expected.
請 here means “to treat”, as in paying for someone.

wordGlosses.english: thank you (for a gift or favour)

lessons.summary: Share some family gossip with a friend, and swear them to secrecy.

content.title: Spill the tea
content.scenario: Share some family gossip with a friend, and swear them to secrecy.

rounds.situation: You can’t wait to share some news with a friend.
rounds.cantonese: 你知唔知呀？我表姐話佢下個月結婚！
rounds.jyutping: nei5 zi1 m4 zi1 aa3 ngo5 biu2 ze2 waa6 keoi5 haa6 go3 jyut6 git3 fan1
rounds.translation: Guess what? My cousin says she’s getting married next month!

chunks.note: Literally “do you know?”. The classic way to open a juicy story.
話 reports what someone said. You’ll hear it in every story.

chunks.jyutping: keoi5 haa6 go3 jyut6 git3 fan1
chunks.note: Cantonese doesn’t need a future tense: the time word does the job.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Open with “guess what” and share your cousin’s big news.

rounds.situation: Add the surprising detail.
rounds.cantonese: 佢哋先至識咗半年咋，好快手喎。
rounds.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 sin1 zi3 sik1 zo2 bun3 nin4 zaa3 hou2 faai3 sau2 wo3
rounds.translation: They’ve only known each other for six months. That’s fast!

chunks.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 sin1 zi3 sik1 zo2 bun3 nin4 zaa3
chunks.english: they’ve only known each other six months
chunks.note: 先至…咋 frames something as surprisingly little: “only just”.
喎 marks something you’ve just noticed and find remarkable.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say they’ve only known each other six months, and react to how fast it is.

rounds.situation: Then your aunt found out.
rounds.cantonese: 跟住佢媽咪聽到，即刻打畀我問長問短。
rounds.jyutping: gan1 zyu6 keoi5 maa1 mi4 teng1 dou2 zik1 hak1 daa2 bei2 ngo5 man6 coeng4 man6 dyun2
rounds.translation: Then her mum heard and immediately called me with a million questions.

chunks.jyutping: gan1 zyu6 keoi5 maa1 mi4 teng1 dou2
chunks.note: 跟住 moves a story forward: “and then…”.
打畀 + person means to phone someone.
A four-character expression: asking about everything, long and short.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Describe how your aunt heard and called you right away.

responseExercise.promptTranslation: Then her mum heard and immediately called me with a million questions.

options.englishTranslation: Then her mum heard and was too upset to call anyone.

rounds.situation: Confess what you told your aunt.
rounds.cantonese: 我話我都唔知，其實我早就知道㗎喇。
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 waa6 ngo5 dou1 m4 zi1 kei4 sat6 ngo5 zou2 zau6 zi1 dou3 gaa3 laa3
rounds.translation: I told her I had no idea, but actually I knew ages ago.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 waa6 ngo5 dou1 m4 zi1
chunks.english: I said I didn’t know either
chunks.note: Reported speech is easy: 我話 + what you said.

chunks.jyutping: kei4 sat6 ngo5 zou2 zau6 zi1 dou3 gaa3 laa3
chunks.note: 其實 introduces the truth. 㗎喇 adds a cheeky “for a while now”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Admit you pretended not to know, but actually knew long ago.

rounds.situation: Swear your friend to secrecy.
rounds.cantonese: 你千祈唔好講出去呀，我會畀佢鬧死！
rounds.jyutping: nei5 cin1 kei4 m4 hou2 gong2 ceot1 heoi3 aa3 ngo5 wui5 bei2 keoi5 naau6 sei2
rounds.translation: Whatever you do, don’t tell anyone, or she’ll kill me!

chunks.jyutping: nei5 cin1 kei4 m4 hou2 gong2 ceot1 heoi3 aa3
chunks.english: whatever you do, don’t tell anyone
chunks.note: 千祈唔好 is a strong, pleading “never ever”.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 wui5 bei2 keoi5 naau6 sei2
chunks.note: 畀 + person + verb is the passive: “get scolded by her”. 死 just exaggerates.

wordGlosses.english: tell off badly (lit. scold to death)

lessons.summary: Debate the Hong Kong property question with a friend, then agree to disagree.

content.title: Rent or buy?
content.scenario: Debate the Hong Kong property question with a friend, then agree to disagree.

rounds.situation: Over dinner, a friend asks if you’d buy a flat.
rounds.cantonese: 我覺得而家買樓唔抵，租樓仲好啲。
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 gok3 dak1 ji4 gaa1 maai5 lau2 m4 dai2 zou1 lau2 zung6 hou2 di1
rounds.translation: I think buying a flat isn’t worth it right now; renting is better.

chunks.note: The go-to opener for any opinion.

chunks.jyutping: ji4 gaa1 maai5 lau2 m4 dai2
chunks.english: buying a flat isn’t worth it now
chunks.note: 抵 means good value. 唔抵 is a very Hong Kong judgement.
仲 + adjective + 啲 means “even better”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Give your opinion: renting beats buying right now.

rounds.situation: Your friend pushes back.
rounds.cantonese: 係咩？但係租金咁貴，好似幫業主供樓咁。
rounds.jyutping: hai6 me1 daan6 hai6 zou1 gam1 gam3 gwai3 hou2 ci5 bong1 jip6 zyu2 gung1 lau2 gam3
rounds.translation: Really? But rent is so expensive, it’s like paying the landlord’s mortgage.

chunks.note: A doubtful “is that so?”. 咩 signals surprise or disbelief.

chunks.jyutping: daan6 hai6 zou1 gam1 gam3 gwai3
chunks.note: 咁 + adjective means “so…”.

chunks.jyutping: hou2 ci5 bong1 jip6 zyu2 gung1 lau2 gam3
chunks.note: A classic Hong Kong complaint about renting.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Push back: rent is so high you’re basically paying the landlord’s mortgage.

rounds.situation: Give some ground, but hold your point.
rounds.cantonese: 你講得啱，不過供樓壓力實在太大。
rounds.jyutping: nei5 gong2 dak1 ngaam1 bat1 gwo3 gung1 lau2 aat3 lik6 sat6 zoi6 taai3 daai6
rounds.translation: You have a point, but the pressure of a mortgage is just too much.

chunks.note: Concede first, then disagree: it keeps the conversation friendly.

chunks.jyutping: bat1 gwo3 gung1 lau2 aat3 lik6
chunks.note: 不過 is a softer “but” than 但係.
實在 adds emphasis: “really, honestly”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Admit they have a point, then say a mortgage is too stressful.

responseExercise.promptCantonese: 你講得啱，不過供樓壓力實在太大。
responseExercise.promptJyutping: nei5 gong2 dak1 ngaam1 bat1 gwo3 gung1 lau2 aat3 lik6 sat6 zoi6 taai3 daai6
responseExercise.promptTranslation: You have a point, but the pressure of a mortgage is just too much.

options.englishTranslation: You have a point, but the pressure of a mortgage is just too much.
You have a point, and my landlord is actually really nice.
You have a point, and rent keeps going up every year.

rounds.situation: Keep it friendly.
rounds.cantonese: 我唔係話你錯，只係大家諗法唔同啫。
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 m4 hai6 waa6 nei5 co3 zi2 hai6 daai6 gaa1 nam2 faat3 m4 tung4 ze1
rounds.translation: I’m not saying you’re wrong, we just see it differently.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 m4 hai6 waa6 nei5 co3
chunks.note: A useful softener before any disagreement.

chunks.jyutping: zi2 hai6 daai6 gaa1 nam2 faat3 m4 tung4 ze1
chunks.note: 啫 downplays things: “that’s all, no big deal”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you’re not calling them wrong, you just think differently.

rounds.situation: Time to change the subject.
rounds.cantonese: 好啦，今晚唔好再嘈喇，飲杯先！
rounds.jyutping: hou2 laa1 gam1 maan1 m4 hou2 zoi3 cou4 laa3 jam2 bui1 sin1
rounds.translation: Okay, no more arguing tonight. Let’s have a drink first!

chunks.note: 啦 here wraps up the discussion.

chunks.jyutping: gam1 maan1 m4 hou2 zoi3 cou4 laa3
chunks.note: 嘈 means noisy, and also arguing loudly.
Ending with 先 means “let’s do this first, the rest later”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: End the debate and suggest a drink.

rounds.situation: Monday morning. A friend asks about your weekend.

rounds.jyutping: gam1 go3 weekend nei5 zou6 zo2 di1 mat1 je5 hou2 waan2 aa3

content.title: Grandma’s soup
content.scenario: Learn Grandma’s slow-cooked soup, step by step, in her kitchen.

rounds.situation: You ask Grandma to teach you her signature soup.
rounds.cantonese: 婆婆，你教我煲你個招牌老火湯好唔好？
rounds.jyutping: po4 po2 nei5 gaau3 ngo5 bou1 nei5 go3 ziu1 paai4 lou5 fo2 tong1 hou2 m4 hou2
rounds.translation: Grandma, can you teach me how to make your famous slow-cooked soup?

chunks.note: 婆婆 is your mother’s mother. Your father’s mother is 嫲嫲.
煲 is the word for slow-cooking soup in a pot.

chunks.cantonese: 你個招牌老火湯好唔好
chunks.jyutping: nei5 go3 ziu1 paai4 lou5 fo2 tong1 hou2 m4 hou2
chunks.note: 老火湯 simmers for hours. Ending with 好唔好 makes it a sweet request.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask Grandma to teach you her signature soup.

rounds.situation: Grandma starts with the bones.
rounds.cantonese: 首先將啲豬骨飛一飛水，再放落煲度。
rounds.jyutping: sau2 sin1 zoeng1 di1 zyu1 gwat1 fei1 jat1 fei1 seoi2 zoi3 fong3 lok6 bou1 dou6
rounds.translation: First, blanch the pork bones quickly, then put them in the pot.

chunks.jyutping: sau2 sin1 zoeng1 di1 zyu1 gwat1
chunks.note: 將 moves the object to the front, like “take X and…”.
飛水 is kitchen talk for blanching. Doubling the verb makes it quick and casual.

chunks.english: then put them in the pot
chunks.note: 放落…度 means “put down into…”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Explain the first step: blanch the pork bones, then into the pot.

rounds.situation: She warns you about the heat.
rounds.cantonese: 火唔好太大，要慢慢煲足三個鐘。
rounds.jyutping: fo2 m4 hou2 taai3 daai6 jiu3 maan6 maan2 bou1 zuk1 saam1 go3 zung1
rounds.translation: Don’t make the heat too high; let it simmer slowly for a full three hours.

chunks.english: don’t make the heat too high
chunks.note: 唔好 + adjective is a gentle warning.

chunks.jyutping: jiu3 maan6 maan2 bou1 zuk1 saam1 go3 zung1
chunks.english: simmer slowly for a full three hours
chunks.note: 足 means “a full…”. 個鐘 is the everyday word for hour.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Pass on Grandma’s tip: low heat, a full three hours.

responseExercise.promptJyutping: fo2 m4 hou2 taai3 daai6 jiu3 maan6 maan2 bou1 zuk1 saam1 go3 zung1
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Don’t make the heat too high; let it simmer slowly for a full three hours.

options.englishTranslation: Turn the heat up high so it’s ready in three hours.

rounds.situation: The secret is in the timing.
rounds.cantonese: 鹽要最後先落，唔係就會太鹹。
rounds.jyutping: jim4 jiu3 zeoi3 hau6 sin1 lok6 m4 hai6 zau6 wui5 taai3 haam4
rounds.translation: Add the salt only at the very end, otherwise it’ll be too salty.

chunks.jyutping: jim4 jiu3 zeoi3 hau6 sin1 lok6
chunks.english: add the salt only at the end
chunks.note: 最後先 means “not until the end”. 落 means to add an ingredient.

chunks.jyutping: m4 hai6 zau6 wui5 taai3 haam4
chunks.note: 唔係 here means “otherwise”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Explain when to add the salt and why.

rounds.situation: Three hours later, you taste your soup.
rounds.cantonese: 嘩，好清甜呀！同你煲嘅一樣咁好飲。
rounds.jyutping: waa3 hou2 cing1 tim4 aa3 tung4 nei5 bou1 ge3 jat1 joeng6 gam3 hou2 jam2
rounds.translation: Wow, it’s so light and sweet! It tastes just as good as yours.

chunks.note: 清甜 is the highest praise for soup: clean, naturally sweet.

chunks.jyutping: tung4 nei5 bou1 ge3 jat1 joeng6 gam3 hou2 jam2
chunks.note: 同…一樣咁 + adjective means “just as … as”. Soup is 好飲, not 好食.

lessons.summary: Chat with your cousin about a drama everyone is talking about, and plan a concert night.

content.title: TVB and Cantopop
content.scenario: Chat with your cousin about a drama everyone is talking about, and plan a concert night.

rounds.situation: Your cousin asks about the latest drama.
rounds.cantonese: 你有冇追緊嗰套新嘅TVB劇呀？
rounds.jyutping: nei5 jau5 mou5 zeoi1 gan2 go2 tou3 san1 ge3 TVB kek6 aa3
rounds.translation: Have you been following that new TVB drama?

chunks.note: 追劇 means to binge or follow a show. 緊 shows it’s ongoing.

chunks.jyutping: go2 tou3 san1 ge3 TVB kek6
chunks.note: 套 is the counter for series and films. TVB dramas are a shared family ritual.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask your cousin if they’re watching the new TVB drama.

rounds.situation: You’re hooked.
rounds.cantonese: 有呀，我晚晚都準時八點半等住睇。
rounds.jyutping: jau5 aa3 ngo5 maan5 maan5 dou1 zeon2 si4 baat3 dim2 bun3 dang2 zyu6 tai2
rounds.translation: Yes! Every night I’m waiting to watch at 8:30 sharp.

chunks.note: Answer a 有冇 question with 有 or 冇.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 maan5 maan5 dou1 zeon2 si4 baat3 dim2 bun3
chunks.note: Doubling a time word (晚晚, 日日) means “every”.
住 shows a continuing state: sitting there waiting.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you watch every night at 8:30 sharp.

rounds.situation: Your cousin has heard a spoiler about the finale.
rounds.cantonese: 聽講下個禮拜大結局好爛尾，啲觀眾已經嬲到投訴！
rounds.jyutping: teng1 gong2 haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 daai6 git3 guk6 hou2 laan6 mei5 di1 gun1 zung3 ji5 ging1 nau1 dou3 tau4 sou3
rounds.translation: I heard next week’s finale is a total letdown, and viewers are already so angry they’re complaining!

chunks.jyutping: teng1 gong2 haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 daai6 git3 guk6 hou2 laan6 mei5
chunks.english: I heard next week’s finale is a letdown
chunks.note: 大結局 is a series finale. 爛尾 (lit. rotten tail) means a bad ending. Also used for unfinished buildings.

chunks.jyutping: di1 gun1 zung3 ji5 ging1 nau1 dou3 tau4 sou3
chunks.english: viewers are already so angry they’re complaining
chunks.note: 嬲到 + result means “so angry that…”.

rounds.situation: Change the topic to something more fun.

lessons.summary: Run a project meeting in Hong Kong office Cantonese and push back on a tight deadline.

content.title: The deadline meeting
content.scenario: Run a project meeting in Hong Kong office Cantonese and push back on a tight deadline.

rounds.situation: You open the Monday project meeting.
rounds.cantonese: 各位，我哋今日主要傾吓個project嘅進度。
rounds.jyutping: gok3 wai2 ngo5 dei6 gam1 jat6 zyu2 jiu3 king1 haa5 go3 project ge3 zeon3 dou6
rounds.translation: Everyone, today we mainly need to go over the project’s progress.

chunks.note: A polite way to address a group at the start of a meeting.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gam1 jat6 zyu2 jiu3 king1 haa5
chunks.english: today we mainly need to talk over
chunks.note: 傾 is to chat or discuss. 吓 makes it sound light: “have a quick talk”.
Office Cantonese mixes in English words like project, email, check.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Open the meeting and say you’ll go over the project’s progress.

rounds.situation: Share the news from the top.
rounds.cantonese: 老闆想我哋下個禮拜五之前搞掂。
rounds.jyutping: lou5 baan2 soeng2 ngo5 dei6 haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 ng5 zi1 cin4 gaau2 dim6
rounds.translation: The boss wants us to finish it before next Friday.

chunks.note: 老闆 is your boss, or the owner of any shop.

chunks.jyutping: haa6 go3 lai5 baai3 ng5 zi1 cin4
chunks.note: 禮拜 + number is the everyday way to say weekdays.
搞掂 means sorted, finished, handled.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell the team the boss wants it done before next Friday.

rounds.situation: Raise your concern.
rounds.cantonese: 老實講，咁趕嘅話，質素一定會受影響。
rounds.jyutping: lou5 sat6 gong2 gam3 gon2 ge3 waa2 zat1 sou3 jat1 ding6 wui5 sau6 jing2 hoeng2
rounds.translation: Honestly, if it’s that rushed, the quality will definitely suffer.

chunks.note: Starting with 老實講 signals a frank opinion without sounding rude.
…嘅話 means “if…”. 趕 means rushed or in a hurry.

chunks.jyutping: zat1 sou3 jat1 ding6 wui5 sau6 jing2 hoeng2
chunks.note: 受影響 means to be affected.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say honestly that rushing will hurt the quality.

responseExercise.promptCantonese: 老實講，咁趕嘅話，質素一定會受影響。
responseExercise.promptJyutping: lou5 sat6 gong2 gam3 gon2 ge3 waa2 zat1 sou3 jat1 ding6 wui5 sau6 jing2 hoeng2
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Honestly, if it’s that rushed, the quality will definitely suffer.

options.englishTranslation: Honestly, if it’s that rushed, the quality will definitely suffer.

Honestly, the quality is already suffering, even without rushing.

rounds.situation: Offer a solution.
rounds.cantonese: 不如我同客戶再check吓，睇吓可唔可以延遲幾日。
rounds.jyutping: bat1 jyu4 ngo5 tung4 haak3 wu6 zoi3 check haa5 tai2 haa5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 jin4 ci4 gei2 jat6
rounds.translation: How about I check with the client again and see if we can push it back a few days?

chunks.jyutping: bat1 jyu4 ngo5 tung4 haak3 wu6 zoi3 check haa5
chunks.english: how about I check with the client again
chunks.note: 不如 is the polite way to suggest something.

chunks.jyutping: tai2 haa5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5
chunks.note: A verb + 唔 + verb pattern makes a yes/no question: 可唔可以 = can or can’t.

chunks.english: push it back a few days
chunks.note: 幾 + measure means “a few”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Suggest checking with the client about a few extra days.

rounds.situation: The manager agrees.
rounds.cantonese: 冇問題，有咩update就send個email畀大家。
rounds.jyutping: mou5 man6 tai4 jau5 me1 update zau6 send go3 email bei2 daai6 gaa1
rounds.translation: No problem. If there’s any update, send everyone an email.

chunks.note: The standard way to agree in the office.
有咩…就… means “if anything comes up, then…”.

chunks.jyutping: send go3 email bei2 daai6 gaa1
chunks.note: 畀 + person means “to someone”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Agree, and ask for an email to everyone with any update.

No problem. Once the email is sent, call everyone too.

lessons.summary: Forget your anniversary, apologise properly, and make it up to your partner.

content.title: Making up
content.scenario: Forget your anniversary, apologise properly, and make it up to your partner.

rounds.situation: You realise you forgot something important.
rounds.cantonese: BB，對唔住呀，我真係唔記得咗今日係紀念日。
rounds.jyutping: BB deoi3 m4 zyu6 aa3 ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 gei3 dak1 zo2 gam1 jat6 hai6 gei2 nim6 jat6
rounds.translation: Babe, I’m so sorry, I really forgot today is our anniversary.

chunks.note: Couples in Hong Kong often call each other BB (said bi-bi).
對唔住 is a real apology for doing wrong. 唔好意思 is only for small slips.

chunks.cantonese: 我真係唔記得咗今日係紀念日
chunks.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 gei3 dak1 zo2 gam1 jat6 hai6 gei2 nim6 jat6
chunks.english: I really forgot today is our anniversary
chunks.note: 唔記得咗 means “forgot”: 咗 marks it as done.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Apologise to your partner for forgetting your anniversary.

rounds.situation: Own it completely.
rounds.cantonese: 我知你好失望，係我唔啱，你鬧我啦。
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 zi1 nei5 hou2 sat1 mong6 hai6 ngo5 m4 ngaam1 nei5 naau6 ngo5 laa1
rounds.translation: I know you’re really disappointed. It’s my fault, go ahead and tell me off.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 zi1 nei5 hou2 sat1 mong6
chunks.note: Naming their feeling first shows you get it.
唔啱 means wrong or in the wrong.

chunks.english: go ahead and tell me off
chunks.note: 啦 here invites them to do it: “go on”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Acknowledge their disappointment and take the blame.

rounds.situation: Your partner tells you what’s really wrong.
rounds.cantonese: 我唔係嬲你唔記得，係覺得你最近好少陪我。
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 m4 hai6 nau1 nei5 m4 gei3 dak1 hai6 gok3 dak1 nei5 zeoi3 gan6 hou2 siu2 pui4 ngo5
rounds.translation: I’m not angry that you forgot, I just feel you’ve hardly spent time with me lately.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 m4 hai6 nau1 nei5 m4 gei3 dak1
chunks.english: I’m not angry that you forgot
chunks.note: 嬲 is the everyday Cantonese word for angry.

chunks.cantonese: 係覺得你最近好少陪我
chunks.jyutping: hai6 gok3 dak1 nei5 zeoi3 gan6 hou2 siu2 pui4 ngo5
chunks.english: I feel you’ve hardly spent time with me lately
chunks.note: 唔係…係… means “it’s not…, it’s…”. 陪 means to keep someone company.

No past tense needed: context does the work.
冷落 (lit. leave out in the cold) means to neglect someone.

rounds.situation: Make it up to them.

chunks.note: 請假 means to take leave. 咗 shows it’s already arranged.

lessons.summary: Ask Grandpa how he came to Canada and hear his story in his own words.

content.title: Grandpa’s story
content.scenario: Ask Grandpa how he came to Canada and hear his story in his own words.

rounds.situation: You sit with Grandpa after dinner.
rounds.cantonese: 爺爺，你當年點解會嚟加拿大㗎？
rounds.jyutping: je4 je2 nei5 dong1 nin4 dim2 gaai2 wui5 lai4 gaa1 naa4 daai6 gaa3
rounds.translation: Grandpa, why did you come to Canada back then?

chunks.note: 爺爺 is your father’s father. Your mother’s father is 公公.

chunks.jyutping: nei5 dong1 nin4 dim2 gaai2 wui5
chunks.note: 當年 means “in those years”: perfect for family stories.
㗎 at the end shows genuine curiosity.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask Grandpa why he came to Canada back then.

rounds.situation: Grandpa remembers.
rounds.cantonese: 嗰陣時好窮，想搵多啲錢養屋企人。
rounds.jyutping: go2 zan6 si4 hou2 kung4 soeng2 wan2 do1 di1 cin2 joeng5 uk1 kei2 jan4
rounds.translation: We were very poor back then. I wanted to earn more money to support the family.

chunks.english: we were very poor back then
chunks.note: 嗰陣時 sets the scene in the past.
搵錢 is the everyday way to say earn money.
養 means to feed and support.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Retell why Grandpa left: poverty and supporting the family.

rounds.situation: He describes arriving.
rounds.cantonese: 我一個人坐飛機過嚟，一句英文都唔識講。
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 go3 jan1 co5 fei1 gei1 gwo3 lai4 jat1 geoi3 jing1 man2 dou1 m4 sik1 gong2
rounds.translation: I came over on a plane all by myself, and I couldn’t speak a single word of English.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 go3 jan1 co5 fei1 gei1 gwo3 lai4
chunks.english: I came over on a plane all by myself
chunks.note: 一個人 means alone. 過嚟 means “come over (here)”.

chunks.jyutping: jat1 geoi3 jing1 man2 dou1 m4 sik1 gong2
chunks.english: couldn’t speak a word of English
chunks.note: 一 + measure + 都 + negative means “not even one”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Retell how Grandpa arrived: alone, with no English at all.

I came over on a plane all by myself, and I couldn’t speak a single word of English.

rounds.situation: His first job.
rounds.cantonese: 最初喺餐館洗碗，日日做十幾個鐘。
rounds.jyutping: zeoi3 co1 hai2 caan1 gun2 sai2 wun2 jat6 jat6 zou6 sap6 gei2 go3 zung1

chunks.note: 最初 means “at the very beginning”.

chunks.jyutping: jat6 jat6 zou6 sap6 gei2 go3 zung1
chunks.english: worked over ten hours every day
chunks.note: 十幾 means “ten-something”: a little over ten.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Describe Grandpa’s first job and his long hours.

rounds.situation: Grandpa sums it up.
rounds.cantonese: 辛苦係辛苦，但係見到你哋大個，值得㗎。
rounds.jyutping: san1 fu2 hai6 san1 fu2 daan6 hai6 gin3 dou2 nei5 dei6 daai6 go3 zik6 dak1 gaa3
rounds.translation: It was hard, sure, but seeing you all grow up made it worth it.

chunks.note: X係X, 但係… means “X, sure, but…”: admit it, then turn it around.

chunks.jyutping: daan6 hai6 gin3 dou2 nei5 dei6 daai6 go3
chunks.english: but seeing you all grow up
chunks.note: 大個 means grown up.
㗎 makes it firm and heartfelt.

lessons.summary: Give a best-friend toast at a Hong Kong wedding banquet.

content.title: The wedding toast
content.scenario: Give a best-friend toast at a Hong Kong wedding banquet.

rounds.situation: You take the microphone at the banquet.
rounds.cantonese: 各位來賓，多謝大家今晚嚟飲新郎新娘嘅喜酒。
rounds.jyutping: gok3 wai2 loi4 ban1 do1 ze6 daai6 gaa1 gam1 maan1 lai4 jam2 san1 long4 san1 noeng2 ge3 hei2 zau2
rounds.translation: Dear guests, thank you all for coming to the bride and groom’s wedding banquet tonight.

chunks.note: The formal opener for any speech.

chunks.jyutping: do1 ze6 daai6 gaa1 gam1 maan1 lai4
chunks.english: thank you all for coming tonight
chunks.note: 多謝 + person + action thanks them for it.

chunks.jyutping: jam2 san1 long4 san1 noeng2 ge3 hei2 zau2
chunks.english: the bride and groom’s wedding banquet
chunks.note: You “drink” a wedding: 飲喜酒 means attending the banquet.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Open your toast by thanking the guests for coming.

rounds.situation: Talk about your friend, the groom.
rounds.cantonese: 我同新郎識咗十幾年，佢由細到大都好生性。
rounds.jyutping: ngo5 tung4 san1 long4 sik1 zo2 sap6 gei2 nin4 keoi5 jau4 sai3 dou3 daai6 dou1 hou2 saang1 sing3
rounds.translation: I’ve known the groom for over ten years. He’s always been a good, sensible guy.

chunks.jyutping: ngo5 tung4 san1 long4 sik1 zo2 sap6 gei2 nin4
chunks.english: I’ve known the groom for over ten years
chunks.note: 識 means to know a person.
由細到大 means “from childhood until now”.
生性 is what elders say about a well-behaved, responsible young person.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say how long you’ve known the groom and what kind of person he is.

rounds.situation: Now the sweet part.
rounds.cantonese: 不過佢識咗新娘之後，成個人開心咗好多。
rounds.jyutping: bat1 gwo3 keoi5 sik1 zo2 san1 noeng2 zi1 hau6 seng4 go3 jan4 hoi1 sam1 zo2 hou2 do1
rounds.translation: But since he met the bride, he’s been so much happier.

chunks.jyutping: bat1 gwo3 keoi5 sik1 zo2 san1 noeng2 zi1 hau6
chunks.english: but since he met the bride
chunks.note: …之後 means “after…”.

chunks.jyutping: seng4 go3 jan4 hoi1 sam1 zo2 hou2 do1
chunks.note: 成個人 means the whole person. Adjective + 咗好多 means “a lot more…”.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say the groom has been much happier since meeting the bride.

responseExercise.promptCantonese: 不過佢識咗新娘之後，成個人開心咗好多。
responseExercise.promptJyutping: bat1 gwo3 keoi5 sik1 zo2 san1 noeng2 zi1 hau6 seng4 go3 jan4 hoi1 sam1 zo2 hou2 do1
responseExercise.promptTranslation: But since he met the bride, he’s been so much happier.

options.englishTranslation: But since he met the bride, he’s been so much happier.
But since he met the bride, he’s become a lot busier.
But before he met the bride, he was much happier.

rounds.situation: The traditional wedding blessing.
rounds.cantonese: 祝你哋百年好合，早生貴子！
rounds.jyutping: zuk1 nei5 dei6 baak3 nin4 hou2 hap6 zou2 saang1 gwai3 zi2
rounds.translation: Wishing you a lifetime of happiness together, and a baby soon!

chunks.note: 祝 + person + blessing is how every toast and card works.
The classic wedding blessing.
A cheeky, traditional blessing. Expect the elders to cheer.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Give the couple the two classic wedding blessings.

rounds.situation: Raise the room.
rounds.cantonese: 嚟，大家一齊起身舉杯，飲勝！
rounds.jyutping: lai4 daai6 gaa1 jat1 cai4 hei2 san1 geoi2 bui1 jam2 sing3
rounds.translation: Come on, everyone stand up and raise your glasses. Cheers!

chunks.note: 嚟 at the start rallies people: “come on!”.

chunks.jyutping: daai6 gaa1 jat1 cai4 hei2 san1 geoi2 bui1
chunks.english: everyone stand up and raise your glasses
chunks.note: 一齊 means together.
飲勝 is the Cantonese toast. Shout it loud!

rounds.speakingPrompt: Get everyone up for the toast and say cheers.

Come on, everyone stand up and clap for the couple!
